text:
carol (Support): customer reports partial chat output over both SSE and websocket when traffic goes through their corporate edge/proxy + our Fastly edge. request id=req-0a1b2c3d session=sess_8f3a. they see first 1-2 chunks then silence for ~20s, then rest arrives in a burst. hitting origin directly (bypassing Fastly) returns steady streaming.

alice (Support Eng): thanks — can you paste the curl repro you ran against the edge and the direct origin? also confirm client types (browser, mobile, server).

carol (Support): repros attached from customer: mobile web (iOS WKWebView) and a Node-based server proxy. curl against edge:
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat?session=sess_8f3a\'
```
against origin (origin-redwood.example) same curl returns no stalls.

ben (Infra): assigning to infra triage. please collect the following from the customer: 1) full X-Request-Id header values for both edge and origin hits 2) any edge trace ids (Fastly or cf-ray) 3) a small tcpdump/pcap showing timing (they can filter by host/port) 4) origin server logs for req-0a1b2c3d 5) their corporate proxy config (nginx/HAProxy) if available.

carol (Support): they provided this origin log snippet for req-0a1b2c3d:
```
[2026-02-20T12:34:56.123Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d route=/v1/chat status=200 bytes_sent=12345 duration_ms=173 stream_chunks=12 last_chunk_ts=2026-02-20T12:35:15.210Z
```
and this edge (Fastly) log excerpt:
```
fastly: req=req-0a1b2c3d svc=api edge_action=fetch streaming_flush_count=2 last_flush_delta_ms=20468 object_hit=false
```

dave (Runtime Eng): that flush delta ~20s aligns with the silence window. couple hypotheses: 1) proxy/edge coalescing (buffering until N bytes or timeout) 2) HTTP/1.1 chunk coalescing by an intermediate (nginx proxy with proxy_buffering on) 3) client-side buffering (WKWebView has known SSE buffering heuristics). we should try to isolate which side enforces the delay.

alice (Support Eng): quick checks for the customer to run:
- reproduce with wget/curl with --no-buffering (curl -N) and capture verbose headers: curl -v --no-buffer -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat?session=sess_8f3a'
- capture tls/tcp timing: sudo tcpdump -w dump.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443 (send pcap) OR ngrep against decrypted traffic if they can run on proxy (ngrep -W byline -q -d any 'HTTP' tcp and port 443)
- on their node proxy set proxy_buffering off / chunked_transfer_encoding on if using nginx.

carol (Support): customer sent a small tcpdump (timestamps only) that shows no data after initial chunk until ~20s then a burst. they can't share TLS payload. they did share their nginx fragment:
```
proxy_buffering on;
proxy_buffers 8 4k;
proxy_max_temp_file_size 0;
proxy_set_header Connection '';
```
(looks default-ish)

ben (Infra): proxy_buffering on is a suspect. nginx will buffer and try to coalesce. ask them to set proxy_buffering off for that route and re-test. also request we get the Fastly real-time debug logs for req-0a1b2c3d (edge trace id unknown — ask customer to include the Fastly headers).

carol (Support): customer says they can toggle proxy settings but want us to try to reproduce from our side using a synthetic nginx config + Fastly replica. dave, can runtime produce a small load generator to stream SSE with small frequent chunks so we can hit edge+nginx in front and reproduce locally?

dave (Runtime Eng): I can spin a small test service that emits a token every 200ms for 30s (chunked, SSE). attaching sample node script to reproduce:
```
// node sse test
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req,res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache' });
  let i=0;
  const iv = setInterval(() => {
    i++;
    res.write('data: token-'+i+'\n\n');
    if (i>150) { clearInterval(iv); res.end(); }
  }, 200);
}).listen(9000);
```

dave (Runtime Eng): I'll put that behind an nginx replica with proxy_buffering on/off and hit via our staging Fastly to see if stall reproduces.

alice (Support Eng): Meanwhile, carol please get these from the customer and upload a debug bundle:
- curl -v output to text file (redirect stderr)
- tcpdump pcap (timestamps)
- nginx conf fragment + version
- exact X-Request-Id values they saw on both edge and origin hits

carol (Support): they uploaded files to a secure link (internal ticket). X-Request-Id values: req-0a1b2c3d (edge), req-0a1b2c3d-orig (origin). fastly header cf-ray: fr0st-abc123 (they redacted a bit).

ben (Infra): thanks — I'm pulling Fastly debug for fr0st-abc123 and req-0a1b2c3d. if we see the edge shutting the connection or coalescing on origin->edge path that'll point to Fastly config. if Fastly shows steady passthrough but nginx buffers then we'll point to customer's proxy.

support-bot: new debug bundle created: bundle-20260220-1765556789 (contains curl.txt, pcap.tgz, nginx.conf, origin_logs.txt)

alice (Support Eng): next actions: 1) dave run the synthetic test and report whether our staging nginx+fastly reproduces 2) ben check Fastly debug and share event timeline 3) carol coordinate with customer to test proxy_buffering off and upload results. I'll prepare a short explainer for customer about why buffering causes the initial tokens to be delayed (TLDR: intermediaries may wait to accumulate output bytes or until a timeout before flushing).

carol (Support): customer will try proxy_buffering off and retest this afternoon and will provide updated traces. thanks all :thumbsup:

alice (Support Eng): assigning to eng-runtime & infra if we confirm reproducer. tagging @dave @ben.
